scenario.title: VYBORG BAY - 5 MAR 1940
intro.text:
VYBORG BAY - 5 MAR 1940

Karelian Isthmus, Finland

The Finns asked for a ceasefire because their front is collapsing. But before peace comes, we have to capture the west bank of Vyborg Bay and the city itself!

ORDERS
After 10 turns control 10/8/6 VH for a BV/V/TV.

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
4x Infantry
1x Anti-Tank (+1)
2x Reconnaissance
3x Artillery (+1)
2x Fighter Aircraft
1x Tactical Bomber
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Raate road opened and the relief column came through before the forest could cut it again. The 163rd's surviving callsigns answered roll call.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-victory.text: Five formations reached the far end of the Raate road. Start with them when you make the new strength return; recovery is still checking the wrecks behind the column.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-tactical.text: Enough of the column came through to meet the order. Several units need vehicles before we can use them again. I've sent their returns to supply.
line.reaction-lose.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-lose.text: The relief road never opened and the 163rd's callsigns disappeared one by one. The surviving column has been reassigned to Vyborg with no time to pretend the forest taught us nothing.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: We kept the guns together at Raate, and they broke the roadblocks. They also drew fire at every halt. I'd like to hear from the surviving battery commanders before we repeat it.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.callback-choice-b.text: The groups you sent into the Raate forests returned by different roads and with different stories. They cleared the flanks, but some reached the rendezvous after the men they were relieving had gone silent.
line.earned-decision.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.earned-decision.text: The core came off the Raate road without losing a formation. A mountain battalion that screened the last convoy has been placed at your disposal before the Vyborg operation.
line.earned-decision.choice.retain-mount: Keep the mountain battalion with the operational group.
Add an experienced eight-strength mountain-infantry detachment to the core.
line.earned-decision.choice.use-raate-in: Use its veterans to refit and instruct the existing formations.
Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give every formation 10 experience.
line.earned-a-response.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.earned-a-response.text: I'll take the mountain battalion. Let their officers inspect our winter equipment; we've had enough of finding out what's wrong after we set off.
line.earned-b-response.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.earned-b-response.text: Assign the veterans to the replacement companies. Give them time to instruct the men before those companies move.
line.scene-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-0.text: These messages give different deadlines. The batteries have an opening hour; the diplomats may stop the fighting. Which change do I pass to the gun crews first?
line.scene-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.scene-1.text: Both. Don't make the battery commanders guess. And find out which crossing can be ready by the attack hour.
line.decision.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.decision.text: The quickest attack may gain ground before the ceasefire. A deliberate crossing will cost less strength, but the war may end while our bridgeheads are still being organised.
Attack across the bay approaches now and exploit every foothold immediately.
Gain 120 prestige for meeting the political deadline and give infantry 15 experience, but receive no replacements or resupply.
line.decision.choice.prepare-the-crossin: Register the guns, secure each crossing site, and advance only behind established support.
Restore every core formation to full strength, fuel, and ammunition and give artillery 15 experience; preparations cost 40 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-a-0.text: Every foothold becomes an assembly area, not a place to stop. The advance continues until the next position or the ceasefire order arrives.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-1.text: I accept the attack. I want confirmation from every battery that it can receive a ceasefire order while firing.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-0.text: Then no unit crosses without support and a way back. If the ceasefire comes while we're preparing, we stop there. I'll answer for the delay.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-1.text: It may come before the first wave moves. Tell headquarters that now, while there's still time for them to object.
line.post-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.post-0.text: The telephone clerks must wake us if the deadline changes. Keep someone by the batteries' line throughout the crossing.
